receipt_policy: Sanitized summaries only; raw transcripts and raw terminal output are not staged.

summary: Proposed THOS command, skill, plugin, MCP, hygiene, retention, and closeout registries.
Recommended command guardrails: no deletion, no reset/rebase/force push, no advisory commits, no unapproved cloud mutation, no secret publication.
Restated that THOS improves operational scaffolding and does not validate GMUT or close gates.
Emphasized that tool availability is not permission and advisory text is not a receipt.
Separated safe cleanup inventory from approval-required deletion, movement, cloud mutation, and automation changes.
Converted v469A dry-lint principles into THOS checks against scaffold-as-proof and dry-run-as-action.
Proposed schema fields for command surfaces, skill registries, plugin/MCP boundaries, runtime checks, and advisory lanes.
Defined cleanup classes and command guardrail fields.
Mapped GMUT dry-lint predicates to THOS workflow checks.
Supported surface inventory, capability tagging, approval gates, retention classes, and blocked-action logging.
Flagged shell bridge limitation as a blocker to local receipt collection, not a reason to fabricate receipt status.
Recommended non-ephemeral read-only lane records and no broad staging.
Supported plugin/MCP/skill boundaries, raw-material retention exclusions, and external mutation approval gates.
Recommended privacy-preserving cleanup manifests and THOS overclaim lints.
Flagged CLI limitation without treating advisory text as local Git receipt.

consensus: v470 THOS starts as an operational scaffold.
No THOS artifact validates GMUT or closes GMUT gates.
Cleanup begins with inventory and approval packets, not deletion.
External writes and destructive actions require explicit separate approval.
